Method of Attack: The malware identified the user’s NetBeans directory, enumerated all the projects, and then embedded a malicious payload in project files and build JAR files. The malicious payload ensured that every time a NetBeans project was built, it would get executed, further ensuring the malware’s propagation. When executing, it would drop both payload and command and control software components into JAR files of other applications. This allowed for great diversification and adaptability by the malware operators, as they could change what was being deployed to infected systems should any countermeasures be deployed.
Indicators of Compromise: The malware actively searches for installed NetBeans installations. If found, it integrates itself into the build process of any other project built inside NetBeans, so that it includes itself (the malware) inside of any build software.
